chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt and died, so some of his sons took over what was upon him (his business/estate), and they were assessed a debt on behalf of their father. So they went to his house and bought it. With them were other inheritors, women and men, who had not approved of the sale nor consulted them regarding it. So is there anything upon them regarding that? He (peace be upon him) said: If the house was acquired from that business of his, then they were assessed regarding that business, so it is upon all of them.
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the father's debt if the son used the business to buy the family house?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of collective liability in debt inheritance, specifically addressing the scenario where creditors seize a family home acquired through the deceased's business activities. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if the property was purchased with the proceeds of the business, the debt burden falls upon all heirs collectively, regardless of whether they participated in the transaction or consented to the sale. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that business-derived assets and their associated liabilities are treated as a unified estate, ensuring creditors' rights are preserved across all inheritors.
